metadata.title: Build YES Answer Display with Rain Details

story.iWant: to see clear rain information when rain is expected
story.soThat: I can plan my activities around specific rain times
story.tasks: - Task 1: Create AnswerDisplay component structure (AC: 1) - Task 2: Implement YES answer header display (AC: 1) - Task 3: Create DetailCard component for rain information (AC: 1) - Task 4: Implement rain windows display (AC: 1) - Task 5: Implement peak rain details display (AC: 1) - Task 6: Implement safe windows display (AC: 1) - Task 7: Integrate CloseCallBadge component (AC: 1) - Task 8: Implement glassmorphic styling (AC: 1) - Task 9: Integrate AnswerDisplay into page.tsx (AC: 1) - Task 10: Test YES answer display flow (AC: 1)

story-context.acceptanceCriteria: AC-1: Given the API returns a YES decision (≥50% probability) When the answer is displayed Then "YES, it will rain" is prominently displayed And the location tag displays the searched location (e.g., "📍 San Francisco, CA") above the answer And the location tag uses glassmorphic styling consistent with detail cards And the probability percentage is shown (e.g., "65% chance") And rain windows show all expected rain periods with start/end times And peak rain details show time, intensity, and amount And safe windows are displayed if multiple rain periods exist And close call message appears if probability is 40-49% And all information is clearly organized and readable And the display is responsive across all device sizes

artifact.title: Epic 3 Technical Specification: Simple Answer Experience
artifact.section: AC-4: YES Answer Displays with Complete Details
artifact.snippet: YES answer display requirements: "YES, it will rain" in large text, location tag with 📍 emoji, probability percentage, rain windows with start/end times, peak details (time, intensity, amount), safe windows if multiple periods, close call messaging for 40-49% probability, glassmorphic DetailCard components, responsive design across all device sizes.

artifact.title: Epic 3 Technical Specification
artifact.snippet: AnswerDisplay is a presentational component receiving API response data (RainCheckResponse) and searchedLocation string. No internal state - purely presentational. Conditional logic for YES vs NO rendering. Story 3.4 handles YES only, Story 3.5 will extend for NO answer display.

artifact.title: Epic 3 Technical Specification
artifact.snippet: DetailCard is a reusable presentational component for structured data display. Supported types: 'rain-windows', 'safe-windows', 'peak-details'. Uses glassmorphic styling with backdrop-blur, subtle border, bg-opacity. Based on Shadcn UI Card component with custom glassmorphic styling.

artifact.title: Epic 3 Technical Specification
artifact.snippet: RainCheckResponse interface: willRain (boolean), probability (0-100), rainWindows (RainWindow[]), peakTime (string), intensity (light/moderate/heavy), amount (string), safeWindows (SafeWindow[]), closeCall (boolean). Only rainWindows, peakTime, intensity, amount, safeWindows present for YES answers.

artifact.title: Architecture - Component Structure
artifact.snippet: Components directory structure: /components/ui/ for Shadcn UI base components (button, input, card), /components/ for custom components (AnswerDisplay, DetailCard, LoadingState, CloseCallBadge, etc.). Uses absolute imports with @/ prefix.

artifact.title: Architecture - Naming Conventions
artifact.snippet: Components: PascalCase (AnswerDisplay.tsx, DetailCard.tsx). Functions: camelCase with verb-noun pattern. Types/Interfaces: PascalCase. TypeScript strict mode, no 'any' types allowed.

artifact.title: UX Design Specification
artifact.snippet: Glassmorphic dark mode theme inspired by Linear.app. Tailwind utilities: backdrop-blur-md, bg-white/10, border border-white/20. Subtle, professional aesthetic with high contrast. Apply to location tag and all DetailCard components for visual consistency.

artifact.title: Product Requirements Document
artifact.snippet: Will It Rain delivers radical simplicity: one question, one answer. YES answer provides necessary context (rain windows, peak details) without overwhelming the user. Privacy-first, stateless architecture with no data persistence.

artifact.reason: Defines the API response contract that AnswerDisplay component will consume. Currently contains forecast array with parsed data. Will need update or new interface for YES/NO answer format with willRain, probability, rainWindows, peakTime, intensity, amount, safeWindows, closeCall fields.

Main landing page component where AnswerDisplay will be integrated. Contains state management (location, isLoading, answerData, errorData), API call logic (POST /api/check-rain), and form submission handler. Need to import AnswerDisplay and add conditional rendering based on answerData.

story-context.constraints:
1. Component Type: AnswerDisplay and DetailCard must be presentational components with no internal state management. All data passed via props.
2. TypeScript Strict Mode: All components must use explicit TypeScript interfaces for props. No 'any' types allowed. Import types from types/api.ts.
3. Accessibility: Must include comprehensive JSDoc documentation, ARIA labels where appropriate, semantic HTML structure, and keyboard navigation support.
4. Glassmorphic Styling: Location tag and all DetailCard instances must use identical glassmorphic pattern: backdrop-blur-md, bg-white/10, border border-white/20. Consistent with UX design spec.
5. Responsive Design: All components must be mobile-first responsive using Tailwind breakpoints (sm:, md:, lg:). Test at 320px, 768px, 1024px widths.
6. Component Architecture: Follow LoadingState.tsx pattern - imports ordered (external, internal, types), interface at top, component export with JSDoc, hooks at top of component, helper functions, render.
7. Naming Conventions: Components in PascalCase, files in PascalCase for components, camelCase for functions, PascalCase for interfaces. Use verb-noun pattern for functions.
8. Client Component: AnswerDisplay must use "use client" directive for client-side rendering since it may contain interactive elements in future stories.
9. Import Paths: Use absolute imports with @/ prefix (e.g., @/components/ui/card, @/types/api).
10. Testing Requirements: TypeScript compilation (npm run type-check) and ESLint (npm run lint) must pass with zero errors. Manual browser testing required for visual verification.
11. NO Automated Tests: Epic 3 defers unit tests to Epic 5. Focus on TypeScript, ESLint, and manual browser testing only.
12. CloseCallBadge Dependency: Story 3.6 creates CloseCallBadge component, but Story 3.4 AC requires close call rendering for YES answers with 40-49% probability. Create minimal CloseCallBadge in Story 3.4, enhance in 3.6 if needed.

interface.name: AnswerDisplayProps
interface.notes: Props for AnswerDisplay component. response contains API data with willRain, probability, rain details. searchedLocation is the user-entered location string for display in location tag.

interface.name: DetailCardProps
interface.notes: Props for DetailCard component. title is the card heading. data is union type accepting arrays (rain/safe windows) or object (peak details). type determines rendering logic.

interface.name: RainCheckResponse (Expected Format for Story 3.4)
interface.notes: Expected API response format for YES/NO answers. Current types/api.ts has different format (forecast array). May need to update existing interface or create new one. rainWindows, peakTime, intensity, amount, safeWindows only present for YES answers (willRain: true).

interface.name: RainWindow
interface.notes: Defines rain window structure with formatted time strings (12-hour AM/PM format).

interface.name: SafeWindow
interface.notes: Defines safe window structure (identical to RainWindow). Only present when multiple rain periods exist.

interface.name: CloseCallBadgeProps
interface.notes: Props for CloseCallBadge component. show determines visibility. Displays message: "It's a close call - consider bringing an umbrella just in case" when show is true.

tests.standards: Epic 3 testing standards: TypeScript compilation validation (npm run type-check), ESLint validation (npm run lint), manual browser testing on http://localhost:3000. NO automated unit tests (deferred to Epic 5). Test on Chrome primary, defer Safari/Firefox to Epic 4.7. Responsive testing at 320px (mobile), 768px (tablet), 1024px (desktop). Keyboard accessibility testing (Tab navigation). All tests must pass before marking story complete.
tests.locations: will-it-rain/app/page.tsx - Integration point for AnswerDisplay component will-it-rain/components/AnswerDisplay.tsx - YES answer display component will-it-rain/components/DetailCard.tsx - Reusable detail card component will-it-rain/components/CloseCallBadge.tsx - Close call messaging component
tests.ideas:
Test Idea 1 (AC-1): Submit location with YES answer (≥50% probability). Verify "YES, it will rain" displays in large text, location tag shows "📍 [location]" with glassmorphic styling, probability percentage displays (e.g., "65% chance").
Test Idea 2 (AC-1): Test rain windows display. Verify all rain periods display with formatted start/end times (e.g., "2:00 PM - 5:00 PM"). Test with single rain window and multiple rain windows.
Test Idea 3 (AC-1): Test peak details display. Verify peak time, intensity (light/moderate/heavy), and amount (e.g., "0.2 inches") display in DetailCard with structured layout.
Test Idea 4 (AC-1): Test safe windows display. Verify safe windows only display when multiple rain periods exist. Verify correct time formatting. Test scenario with no safe windows (single rain period).
Test Idea 5 (AC-1): Test close call messaging. Submit location with 40-49% probability. Verify close call message displays: "It's a close call - consider bringing an umbrella just in case". Test with 50%+ probability - close call should NOT appear.
Test Idea 6 (AC-1): Test glassmorphic styling. Verify location tag and all DetailCards use backdrop-blur-md, bg-white/10, border border-white/20. Inspect with browser DevTools.
Test Idea 7 (AC-1): Test responsive design. Open browser DevTools responsive mode. Test at 320px (mobile), 768px (tablet), 1024px (desktop). Verify all detail cards display correctly, text is readable, no horizontal scrolling.
Test Idea 8 (TypeScript/ESLint): Run "npm run type-check" - must pass with zero errors. Run "npm run lint" - must pass with zero errors.
Test Idea 9 (Integration): Start dev server (npm run dev). Open http://localhost:3000. Enter location, submit search. Verify smooth transition from loading state to answer display.
Test Idea 10 (Edge Cases): Test with API response containing empty rainWindows array (should handle gracefully). Test with missing safeWindows field (should not display safe windows section).
